page: Microsoft Azure D8ls_v5 is an x86_64 virtual machine positioned within the low-memory tier of the general-purpose D-series family. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this instance allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The underlying architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, backed by vector and cryptographic extensions including AVX-512 and VAES.

Hardware benchmark results position the D8ls_v5 squarely within the mid-range performance band for general computation. Synthetic stress-ng evaluations recorded 1,898.69 for single-core and 7,760.02 for multi-core throughput. In Geekbench testing, the system posted a single-core score of 1,674.0 and a multi-core score of 6,230.0, alongside steady results across software compilation (8,290.0) and ray tracing (9,006.0). Memory subsystems demonstrated read bandwidth of 417.38 GB/sec in small cached blocks and 57.69 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB blocks, with corresponding write speeds reaching 38.67 GB/sec. Across most standardized metrics, including static web serving at 12.59 GB/sec and Redis SET throughput at 8.08 million operations per second, performance remains consistently average, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression landed in the lower 25th percentile.

The D8ls_v5 features no local temporary storage and operates without bundled GPUs, relying entirely on remote managed disks for persistent and non-persistent file storage. The reduced memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-effective alternative to standard 4:1 general-purpose instances for compute-focused applications that do not demand extensive RAM footprints. Tradeoffs include potential memory pressure under concurrent heavy data pipelines and the absence of ephemeral local high-speed scratch drives. This profile makes the instance appropriate for web servers, batch computation, CI/CD compilation runners, microservices hosting, and lightweight application processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D8ls_v5 is a low-memory general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It operates on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz with Hyper-V virtualization and support for AVX-512 vector instructions. The instance provision contains no local disk storage and lacks GPU accelerators, necessitating remote networked disks for all storage operations. Performance across standard CPU and memory benchmarks remains reliably in the median tier, including balanced Geekbench scores, 12.59 GB/sec static web throughput, and 8.08 million Redis operations per second, with multi-threaded bzip3 compression showing weaker results. By curtailing memory density, the D8ls_v5 minimizes compute unit overhead, fitting workloads such as continuous integration build agents, containerized microservices, web hosting, and moderate batch processing tasks.
